items.title: Section: Proper Sleep — Why the Lion King's Posture

items.zh: 又為護持諸臥具故，順世儀故。盡夜初分經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心。從順障法淨修心已，出住處外洗濯其足。洗濯足已，還入住處，如法寢臥，為令寢臥長養大種。得增長已，長益其身，轉有勢力，轉能隨順無間常委善品加行。問：以何因緣右脇而臥？答：與師子王法相似故。問：何法相似？答：如師子王，一切獸中，勇悍堅猛，最為第一。比丘亦爾，於常修習覺寤瑜伽，發勤精進，勇悍堅猛，最為第一。由是因緣，與師子王臥法相似。非如其餘鬼臥、天臥、受欲者臥。由彼一切嬾墮懈怠，下劣精進，勢力薄弱。又法應爾，如師子王右脇臥者，如是臥時，身無掉亂，念無忘失，睡不極重，不見惡夢。異此臥者，與是相違。當知具有一切過失。是故說言：右脇而臥，重累其足。
items.en: Furthermore, to protect one's bedding, and in accordance with worldly custom, one washes the feet after walking and sitting meditation through the whole of the first watch. …Having washed the feet, one returns to the dwelling and lies down properly, so that lying down nourishes the great elements of the body. …Question: For what reason does one lie on the right side? Answer: Because it resembles the posture of the lion king. …Just as the lion king is, among all beasts, the most courageous, firm, and mighty, so too the monk, in constantly cultivating wakeful practice, generates diligence that is most courageous, firm, and mighty; for this reason it is said to resemble the lion king's posture — unlike the posture of a hungry ghost, a god, or one given to lust, all of which come from laziness, inferior diligence, and feeble strength. It is simply so by nature that lying as the lion king does, on the right side, the body does not thrash about, mindfulness is not lost, sleep is not excessively heavy, and no bad dreams appear. Lying otherwise brings the opposite — know that it carries every one of these faults. It is therefore said: one lies on the right side, one leg resting upon the other.

items.title: Sleeping with the Perception of Light Still Present

items.zh: 云何名為住光明想巧便而臥？謂於光明想善巧精懇，善取善思善、了善達，思惟諸天光明俱心，巧便而臥。由是因緣，雖復寢臥，心不惛闇。
items.en: What is meant by lying down skilfully while abiding in the perception of light? It means being skilful and earnest regarding the mark of light — skilfully grasping it, skilfully reflecting on it, skilfully understanding it, skilfully penetrating it — reflecting on the light of the celestial beings with a mind that holds it, and thereby lying down skilfully. By this cause, even while asleep, the mind does not become dark and dull.

items.zh: 如是名為住光明想巧便而臥。

items.title: Lying Down with Mindfulness: Dharma Follows the Mind into Sleep

items.zh: 云何正念巧便而臥？謂若諸法，已聞、已思、已熟修習，體性是善，能引義利。由正念故，乃至睡夢亦常隨轉；由正念故，於睡夢中亦常記憶，令彼法相分明現前，即於彼法心多隨觀；由正念故，隨其所念，或善心眠、或無記心眠。是名正念巧便而臥。
items.en: What is lying down skilfully with mindfulness? It means that teachings already heard, already reflected upon, and already thoroughly cultivated in practice — wholesome in nature, capable of bringing genuine benefit — continue to accompany the mind, through the power of mindfulness, even into sleep and dreams. Through mindfulness, these teachings are also remembered during sleep and dreams, appearing clearly before the mind, which then dwells upon them repeatedly. Through mindfulness, depending on what is held in mind, one sleeps with a wholesome mind, or with a neutral mind. This is called lying down skilfully with mindfulness.

items.title: Lying Down with Clear Comprehension: Catching Afflictions Even in Sleep

items.zh: 云何正知巧便而臥？謂由正念而寢臥時，若有隨一煩惱現前，染惱其心。於此煩惱現生起時，能正覺了，令不堅著，速疾棄捨，既通達已，令心轉還。是名正知巧便而臥。
items.en: What is lying down skilfully with clear comprehension? It means that, while lying down with mindfulness, if any affliction should appear and defile the mind, one correctly recognises it the moment it arises, does not cling to it firmly, swiftly abandons it, and, having thoroughly understood it, brings the mind back. This is called lying down skilfully with clear comprehension.

items.title: Section: Forming the Intention to Rise — The Deer's Alertness

items.zh: 云何名為思惟起想巧便而臥？謂以精進策勵其心，然後寢臥。於寢臥時，時時覺寤，如林野鹿，不應一切縱放其心，隨順、趣向、臨入睡眠。復作是念：我今應於諸佛所許覺寤瑜伽，一切皆當具足成辦。為成辦故，應住精勤最極濃厚加行欲樂。復作是念：我今為修覺寤瑜伽，應正發起勤精進住。為欲修習諸善法故，應正翹勤，離諸嬾墮，起發具足。過今夜分至明清旦，倍增發起勤精進住，起發具足。當知此中，由第一思惟起想，無重睡眠，於應起時速疾能起，終不過時方乃覺寤。由第二思惟起想，能於諸佛共所聽許師子王臥如法而臥，無增無減。由第三思惟起想，令善欲樂常無懈廢。雖有失念，而能後後展轉受學，令無斷絕。如是名為思惟起想巧便而臥。
items.en: What is meant by lying down skilfully while forming the intention to rise? It means spurring on the mind with diligence before lying down. While lying down, one wakes readily again and again, like a deer in the wild forest, and should not let the mind go slack, following, tending towards, and falling into heavy sleep. One further thinks: I should now fully accomplish every part of the wakeful practice permitted by all Buddhas. …Once this night has passed into the bright morning, I shall redouble my diligence, generating it in full. Know that through the first such intention, sleep is not heavy, and one rises swiftly and promptly when it is time, never oversleeping. Through the second, one lies as all Buddhas together permit — the lion king's posture — properly, neither adding to it nor falling short of it. Through the third, the aspiration towards wholesome states never grows slack; even if mindfulness is momentarily lost, one takes it up again and again afterwards, so that it is never truly broken. This is called lying down skilfully while forming the intention to rise.

items.zh: 云何至夜後分速疾覺寤，經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心？夜後分者，謂夜四分中，過後一分，名夜後分。

items.title: Waking Swiftly in the Last Watch

items.zh: 彼由如是住光明想、正念、正知、思惟起想巧便而臥，於夜中分、夜四分中，過於一分，正習睡眠。令於起時，身有堪能應時而起。非為上品惛沈睡眠纏所制伏，令將起時闇鈍、薄弱、嬾墮、懈怠。由無如是闇鈍、薄弱、嬾墮、懈怠，暫作意時，無有艱難，速疾能起。從諸障法淨修心者，如前應知。
items.en: Because one properly sleeps through the middle watch — the middle of the night's four divisions, once the first has passed — abiding in the perception of light, mindfulness, clear comprehension, and the intention to rise, the body is capable of rising promptly when it is time, not overcome by heavy sloth-and-torpor, and not dull, weak, lazy, or idle upon rising. Being free of such dullness, weakness, laziness, and idleness, the moment one turns attention to rising, there is no difficulty at all, and one rises swiftly. Purifying the mind of the obstructions from that point on should be understood as explained before.

items.zh: 如是廣辯初夜後夜常勤修習覺寤瑜伽已。復云何知此中略義？

blocks.text: How a practitioner sleeps. Each element: posture, light, mindfulness, clear comprehension, the intention to rise, has its own purpose.

"Why lie on the right side? Because it resembles the posture of the lion king." Master Cháng Bǎi: face down is a ghost's posture, face up a god's, on the left side an indulger's. Lying on the right, "the body does not thrash about, mindfulness is not lost, sleep is not too heavy, and no bad dreams appear." Venerable Miào Jìng: rest restores the four elements.
One falls asleep with the perception of light still present, so sleep is not dark and heavy. Master Cháng Bǎi: this should include the light of the Dharma.

Through mindfulness, the teachings one has heard and reflected on "continue to accompany the mind even into sleep and dreams". Master Cháng Bǎi: sleeping with a neutral mind is like counting breaths: neither good nor bad.

If an affliction arises, even in a dream, "one recognises it the moment it arises, does not cling to it, and swiftly abandons it". Master Cháng Bǎi: on waking, repent before the Buddha and keep practising.

"Spurring on the mind with diligence before lying down." Master Cháng Bǎi: this does not mean not sleeping, but not being attached to sleep. Venerable Miào Jìng: like a deer in the forest, always alert. The treatise distinguishes stages of falling asleep: following, tending towards, falling into. One then wakes "swiftly and promptly" in the last watch.

quiz.q: For what reason does one lie on the right side?
options: because it resembles the posture of the lion king
quiz.why: "Question: For what reason does one lie on the right side? Answer: Because it resembles the posture of the lion king." Venerable Miào Jìng: the lion lies this way, so the practitioner lies this way too.

quiz.q: The text rejects the postures of ghosts, gods, and the lustful. How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe them?
options: all lie on the right side
ghosts lie face down, gods on their backs, the lustful on the left side
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the ghost's posture is face down, like a ghost falling into the lower realms; lying face up is the god's posture; lying on the left side is the posture of one given to lust.

quiz.q: What benefits of the lion posture does the treatise list, and what reason does Master Cháng Bǎi add?
options: the body does not thrash, mindfulness is not lost, sleep is not too heavy, no bad dreams; it does not press on the heart
no need to wash feet; saves time
quiz.why: "The body does not thrash about, mindfulness is not lost, sleep is not excessively heavy, and no bad dreams appear." Master Cháng Bǎi adds that lying on the right side like the lion king does not press on the heart.

quiz.q: In lying down with mindfulness, what does mindfulness accomplish?
options: the wholesome teachings continue even into sleep and dreams, remembered and clearly present
quiz.why: Through mindfulness, these phenomena continue to accompany the mind even into sleep and dreams, remembered and appearing clearly. Venerable Miào Jìng: even in dreams one is still sitting in meditation, practising calm and insight.

quiz.q: In lying down with clear comprehension, what does one do when an affliction appears?
options: recognise it, not cling, swiftly abandon it, and, having understood it, bring the mind back
quiz.why: "One correctly recognises it the moment it arises, does not cling to it firmly, swiftly abandons it, and, having thoroughly understood it, brings the mind back." Venerable Miào Jìng: once you know there is affliction in the mind, turn the mind around and restore its purity.

quiz.q: How do the two masters explain "like a deer in the wild forest"?
options: deer run fast, so rise fast
Miào Jìng: ever alert for fear a lion is coming; Cháng Bǎi: deer are highly alert and wake at any sound
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: like a deer in the forest, always alert in case a lion comes. Master Cháng Bǎi: like a wild deer in the mountains — highly alert, waking at once at any stir.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi divide "following, tending towards, and falling into" sleep?
options: following is the initial stage before heavy sleep; tending towards is the middle stage
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "following" is the initial stage just before entering heavy sleep; "tending towards" is the middle stage heading into it; "falling into" is the last.
